info.title: Mangools API
info.description:
Exact search volumes, related keyword suggestions, SEO difficulty score and other metrics from all Mangools tools.

## Rate limits & quotas

Two independent limits apply:

1. **Burst limit (`reqs-per-short-period`)** — at most 3 requests per sliding window, counted per account (or per device when unauthenticated) and per resource pool (e.g. `serps`, `related-keywords`). For API-key clients (REST, curl, SDKs, automation tools) the window is 30 seconds; requests through the hosted MCP server get a 1-second window. A request over the limit is refused with HTTP 429 and `type: "RateLimit"`; the answer carries `retry_after` in the body and a `Retry-After` header, both the length of the burst window in seconds (30 or 1), so after waiting that long all slots are free again. Refused requests are not counted, and identical requests repeated within 24 hours, except keyword imports, are served from cache and skip both the burst limit and the quota. Send requests one at a time, not in parallel, and leave at least 11 seconds between requests to the same pool: the window check is inclusive on its boundary, so a request exactly 30 seconds after the first one of three is still refused. On a 429 `RateLimit`, wait `retry_after` seconds and send the same request again.
2. **Quota pools** — each paid operation draws from a named pool returned under `resources` in `GET /kwfinder/limits`. Daily pools (e.g. `serps`, `related-keywords`, `sch-url-metrics`, `kw-url-metrics`, `lm-url-metrics`, `sp-overview`, `trends`, `lm-suggest`) run in 24-hour periods: the first counted request starts a period, and when it ends the whole pool is available again; monthly pools (e.g. `links`) reset at the end of the calendar month. Identical requests within 24 hours are served from cache and do not consume quota. Each paid operation declares its pool in an `x-quota-pool` extension. Each pool's `reset` value is the number of seconds remaining until reset (relative, not a unix timestamp).

For API-key clients, the keyword-import endpoint also allows only one import per 30 seconds per account; a faster import answers 429 with `type: "RateLimit"` and `retry_after` set to the seconds left. A spent quota answers 429 with `type: "CreditLimit"`, which never carries `retry_after`.

### Gateway rate limit

Every endpoint sits behind a public gateway that limits the request rate per client IP. A request over that rate is answered by the gateway itself with HTTP 429 and an HTML error page, not the JSON error object documented on the operations below.

get.description:
Get a list of relevant keywords based on your seed keyword. You only need to send your seed keyword. Location and language are optional.

The seed keyword comes first; the other keywords are not sorted by any metric.

### Limits

Each request is counted towards your **Keyword lookups** limit. Lookup is not counted if you make the identical request within 24 hours.

### Locations

You can specify a location_id to get localized search volumes or use `0` for global search volumes.

To get a list of supported locations, please refer to [this article](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/geotargets).

### Languages

To get a list of supported languages, please refer to [this article](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/codes-formats#languages).

### Number of results

Each request returns at most the related-keywords-rows value of your plan (see GET /kwfinder/limits), and never more than 10,000 keywords. Based on a seed keyword, location and language the number of returned keywords may vary.

### Keyword metrics

The result is a list of keywords with metrics such as:
   * CPC
   * PPC
   * Cached keyword difficulty, if exists.
   * Average search volume
   * Search volume history


### Search volumes

Each keyword in a list has an average [search volume](https://mangools.com/kwfinder/features/search-volume/) based on the last 12 months and search volume history. Search volume history length may vary - it may include data since 2015.

post.summary: Get details for a set of keywords
post.description:
This is one of the most powerful endpoints in our API. You can import up to the related-keywords-rows value of your plan (see GET /kwfinder/limits; at least 200 keywords) in one request; a larger set answers HTTP 400.

With this endpoint, you will get the following details for each keyword:

- Cached Keyword SEO difficulty (rank)
- CPC, PPC
- Search volume history
- Average search volume (last 12 months - as `sv` attribute)
- Organic SERP results and CTRs

### Limits

Each request counts as one lookup towards your **Keyword lookups** limit, also when it repeats an earlier import.

### Locations

You can specify a location_id to get localized search volumes and SERPs.

To get a list of supported locations, please refer to [this article](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/data/geotargets).

### How to send keywords
To get data about set of keywords send them in the request body. Don't forget to include location and language ids. See the following example of request body:

    {
       "keywords": [
          "seo agency",
          "seo",
          "seo specialist"
       ],
       "location_id": 21167,
       "language_id": 1000
     }

post.description:
`fields` can be used to filter columns you wish to include in the export.
 possible values include:
   * kw: Keyword
   * sv: Avg. Search Volume
   * lid: Location
   * cpc: Cost per click
   * ppc: PPC competition (0-100)
   * seo: Keyword difficulty
   * msv: Monthly Search Volume

### Prerequisites
The `keyword_ids` are Mangools-specific identifiers returned by keyword-producing endpoints — call one of `/kwfinder/keyword-imports`, `/kwfinder/related-keywords`, `/kwfinder/competitor-keywords`, `/kwfinder/suggested-keywords`, or `/kwfinder/serps` first and reuse the `_id` values (or `mId` for SERP items). IDs that do not correspond to known keywords are silently dropped from the response.


The response is a JSON array of keyword objects. Posting to `/kwfinder/keywords.csv` instead returns the same data as a `text/csv` attachment.

At most 10,000 keyword IDs per request.

post.description:
Find keywords that your competitors rank for but your domain doesn't — the classic SEO content-gap analysis. Compare your domain against up to 5 competitors.

Request body:

* `domain` — your domain to analyze
* `competitors` — array of 1–5 competitor domains
* `location_id` — location for the analysis
* `page` — optional page number (Premium, Agency, Custom and API Pro plans; other plans always get page 1)

The response holds one result per competitor: the keywords that competitor ranks for and your domain does not, ordered by the competitor's position, best first. Each keyword includes search volume, keyword difficulty, CPC and the competitor's position.

### Limits

Each competitor counts as one lookup towards your **Keyword lookups** limit, unless the same domain, competitor, location and page were requested in the last 24 hours.

Authentication is optional on this operation: a request without `X-Access-Token`, or with a token that matches no account, returns HTTP 200 with nothing remaining in any pool rather than HTTP 401. Do not use this operation to validate an API key — use one that requires authentication, such as `GET /kwfinder/requests`.

### Prerequisites
This endpoint requires a prior call to `/serpchecker/serps` for the same query. Pass the `serp_snapshot_id` from that response, **not** the bare `_id`: the snapshot is stored under a key of the form `<id>.<YYYY-MM-DD>` (with `.100` appended for a hundred-result SERP), and that whole key is what this path segment takes. A bare `_id` finds the lookup but not the stored page, and the endpoint answers HTTP 404 `SERP snapshot not found`. A query that was never looked up answers HTTP 404 `Serp not found`.

Get SEO metrics for a specific URL, domain or subdomain — Citation Flow, Trust Flow, referring domain and backlink counts sourced from Majestic. Useful for quickly evaluating a target's link authority before pulling a full backlink profile.

### Limits

Counts toward the daily lm-url-metrics pool in GET /kwfinder/limits. Identical requests within 24 hours are reused from cache.

Use this endpoint to get a list of backlinks for a specific URL, domain or URL path. It returns up to 500 backlinks per page.

To get more backlinks you need to paginate with `page` parameter.

Tip: set `links_per_domain` to `1` to get one backlink per referring domain.

### Limits

Each request is counted towards your **Backlink rows** limit. It is reduced for each returned link.

Create a new rank tracking for a single domain on a specific search location and platform. Pass the target `domain`, an initial list of `keywords`, the `location_id` and `platform_id`. Once the tracking is created, its keywords are queued for SERP crawl and default weekly and monthly email reports are automatically generated.

### Platforms

Use `platform_id` to choose the platform: 1 for desktop, 2 for mobile. For multiple platforms in a single call, see `/serpwatcher/multiple-trackings`.

### Duplicates

A tracking with the same domain, location and platform already in use returns HTTP 409.

get.description:
Get a lightweight snapshot of a tracking together with its tracked keyword list for the requested date range (`from`, `to`). Each keyword includes its id, text, currently ranking URL (as of the latest date), assigned tags and last-check timestamp. Rank history and aggregated statistics are intentionally omitted — use `POST /serpwatcher/trackings/{tracking_id}/stats` for those.

Set `is_with_deleted=true` to include previously deleted keywords.

### Shared access

The endpoint also accepts a read-only `share_token` query parameter, allowing dashboards to be shared without exposing account credentials.

post.description:
Get aggregated rank tracking statistics and per-keyword rank data for a tracking over the requested date range (`from`, `to`).

For each keyword the response contains:

* current rank, best rank and average rank
* rank change and estimated visits deltas
* rank history sampled across the range
* presence and position in Map Pack and Featured Snippet
* detected SERP features
* last-check and last-crawl timestamps

Optionally pass `kwIds` in the request body to limit the response to a specific subset of tracked keywords. The response also includes annotations overlapping the date range.

### Shared access

Unauthorized.description: The `x-access-token` header is missing, malformed or does not match an active API key.

RateLimited.description:
The request was refused by the quota system; `error.type` tells the two cases apart.

**`RateLimit`** — too many requests in a short period (the burst limit, or the keyword-import cooldown). For the burst limit, `retry_after` is the length of the burst window: 30 seconds for API-key clients, 1 second for the hosted MCP server. What to do:

1. Read `error.retry_after` (seconds) or the `Retry-After` header.
2. Wait that many seconds.
3. Send the same request again, once.
4. Keep sending one request at a time, not in parallel.

**`CreditLimit`** — the plan limit for this resource is spent. It never carries `retry_after`, and waiting does not clear it. Do not retry: call `GET /kwfinder/limits` to read the remaining allowance per resource and tell the user the quota is spent.

error.message: Too many requests in short period. Wait retry_after seconds (also sent as the Retry-After header), then send this same request again. Send requests one at a time, not in parallel.
